input: read ./prompt.md and follow the instructions there
task: open-tennis-robots flagship buildable item: a wedge squaring the hopper posts' tops to the sloped shelf

doc_friction.issue: _stack's legacy path for axis 'z' centres a 1400 mm ring at the point's own z (often 0), so a joint above z=700 (the shelf at ~2 m) silently measures nothing; had to pass a Location frame at the joint instead. Not documented on Joint.
test_hopper_posts_stand_on_the_deck_and_meet_the_shelf selected parts by startswith('hopper_post'), which a new part named hopper_post_* silently joins; narrowed to the two names.

goal: Make the feeder's hopper shelf buildable as drawn: full-face contact on its posts and screws that can enter the tapped bores.
notes: Found a second fault behind the 'shim' note: the shelf's laser holes are normal to the 12 deg plate, so its M5s met the posts' vertical bores 12 deg off. Fix: printed PETG wedges (3.0-7.25 mm) on square-cut posts (3 mm shorter), shelf holes 5.5->6.6 mm for vertical M5s, printed taper washers, M5 x 25 (was x16; a new checked joint, 26 joints, 12 mm into a 15 mm tap). check_post_wedge rules each tested firing. Verification: feeder package regenerated (python -m otr_cad feeder, exit 0, 2m42s); cad pytest suite 173 passed in 6 min (first run caught the guide's hard-coded joint count 25, now 26); venture-preflight.mjs open-tennis-robots: 'preflight clean', exit 0.

pricing.source: Anthropic pricing as cached in the Claude API skill (models table and per-model migration notes), 2026-10-06. Cache writes are 1.25x input (5-minute) and 2x input (1-hour); cache reads differ by model.

human_equivalent.basis: a mechanical designer finding the screw-angle fault, drawing a wedge and taper washer, updating BOM/guide and checks
